rv.q: "It’s a scathing, occasionally sidesplitting and not precisely subtle indictment of the Baby Boomer generation and the havoc it has heedlessly wrought...Bartlett occasionally comes at his social and political argument too directly...

"The premise and structure of 'Love, Love, Love' is intriguing: In three acts, with an intermission between each, we leapfrog across the decades...'Love, Love, Love' might have redeemed itself if it contained a modicum of the love its title boasts, or if any of these characters had even the slightest bit of an arc, but they don’t...
